question.leadin: This man's political supporters were derogatorily nicknamed the descamisados, or "shirtless ones."
question.text: Name this populist president of a South American country who regained power in 1973 after being overthrown in 1955. This man legalized women's suffrage while being influenced by his wife, Evita.
question.clue: This politician's left-wing supporters were killed at an airport in the Ezeiza (ayz-ay-EE-zah) massacre.

swap.text: The US also occupied this country after the Spanish-American War, though they did not annex it. The CIA tried to use an exploding cigar and a tuberculosis-infected scuba suit to kill Fidel Castro, a Communist who led this country during the Cold War.
swap.clue: John F. Kennedy said he wanted to "splinter the CIA into a thousand pieces" after a failed invasion of this country at the Bay of Pigs.

question.text: This next largest Caribbean island, the most populous island in the Americas, contains the nations of Haiti and the Dominican Republic.
question.clue: An independence movement on this island called La Trinitaria was led by Juan Pablo Duarte.

swap.text: In the 17th and 18th centuries, galleon trade flourished between Manila and this Mexican city, whose bay forms a notable beach resort today.
swap.clue: This Mexican port city. Under the rule of New Spain, it was granted a monopoly on the Manila galleon trade.

question.leadin: The death of President Francisco Solano Lopez marked the end of this war.
question.text: Name this destructive South American conflict in which a namesake coalition crushed Paraguay and claimed much of its territory.
question.clue: Rutherford Hayes arbitrated a boundary dispute after this war, whose turning point occurred when Admiral Barroso destroyed the enemy fleet at Riachuelo.

swap.leadin: Answer some stuff about the crazy political and military career of Andres de Santa Cruz.
swap.text: Along with Jose Antonio de Sucre, Andres defeated Melchor Aymerich at the Battle of Pichincha freeing this country from Spanish rule. This country's most populous city of Guayaquil was the site of a conference between San Martin and Bolivar.
swap.clue: One peak in this nation, with a name meaning "Smooth Neck of the Moon," is one of the world's highest active volcanoes, while its tallest mountain is known for containing the point farthest from the Earth's surface.

question.leadin: While staying on this island, one leader was warned of an attempted assassination by Jose Antonio Paez.
question.text: Name this island which titles an 1815 "Letter" advocating for Latin American unity. Earlier, this island was the site of Maroon revolts led by Nanny and Cudjoe.
question.clue: Cudjoe and Nanny led escaped slaves on this island in fighting Europeans.

swap.leadin: The control of this country's First Republic by two wealthy states led to it being nicknamed for their main products, "coffee and milk."
swap.text: Name this country, where that republic was founded by disciples of the positivist sociologist Auguste Comte. This country was later ruled by the populist dictator Getulio Vargas.
swap.answerHtml: Brazil [or Federative Republic of Brazil; accept First Brazilian Republic; accept Republic of the United States of Brazil; prompt on Old Republic]
swap.clue: The Constitutionalist Revolution in this country, which demanded one ruler's power be checked, was also known as the Paulista War which, like the Pernambuco Revolt, was named for one of this country's states.

question.text: Revolting twice against Sebastian Lerdo, he took power in 1877 and served as president twice before resigning in 1911 and going into exile.
question.clue: Reforms under this leader were promulgated by technocratic cientificos such as Jose Yves Limantour.

swap.leadin: Answer some questions about the New Deal.
swap.text: This island's namesake "reconstruction administration" was created as part of the New Deal. Its economy was later modernized through Operation Bootstrap.
swap.clue: Revolutionaries from this place uttered the "Grito de Lares" and used the Blair House to stage an unsuccessful assassination attempt on Harry Truman.

question.leadin: Answer the following about charming Latin American dictators.
question.text: This Central American country's leader Efrain Rios Montt ran on the "guns and beans" campaign. The land-redistributing Decree 900 was passed by a slightly less fiendish president of this country, Jacobo Arbenz.
question.clue: Another leader embraced Decree 900, an agrarian reform law opposed by the United Fruit Company, but was later overthrown by the CIA in operation PBSUCCESS.

swap.text: In 1928, banana workers striking for rights at a UFC plantation in this country were killed by the government of Miguel Abadia Mendez. In 1997, Chiquita laborers were held hostage by FARC, a rebel group in this country that signed a 2016 peace deal.
swap.clue: While campaigning for the presidency in this country in 2002, Oxygen Green party candidate Ingrid Betancourt ("bay-tahn-KOOR") was kidnapped by a guerilla group.

question.leadin: Richard Nixon supposedly told Richard Helms to "make the economy scream" in response to the election of this leader.
question.text: Name this leader. Orlando Letelier, this leader's ambassador to the U.S., tried to negotiate the nationalization of his country's copper mines.
question.clue: U.S. officials supported this leader's opponent, Jorge Alessandri, in the presidential election of 1970.

swap.leadin: The Riggs Bank in the U.S. provided multiple false shell companies and methods of allowing this human rights violator of accessing his funds after he was arrested by the British.
swap.text: Identify this South American who led a junta after deposing his democratic predecessor Salvador Allende.
swap.clue: On his 60th birthday, the CIA launched Operation Condor to suppress left-wing movements in this man's nation and neighboring Argentina.

question.leadin: Answer these questions about the popular historical pastime of gun-running.
question.text: Salvador Allende's already-dicey position in Chile was damaged even further by this scandal, in which the namesake containers delivered by aircraft from a friendly regime were discovered to be filled with grenades and machine guns.

swap.leadin: A so-called "republic" named for these people was led by Barbe Blanche and established settlements on the Le Morne peninsula.
swap.text: Name these people who, in a different part of the world, were led by Quao, Zumbi, and Queen Nanny, the last of whom resisted British colonization.
swap.clue: Edward Trelawny ordered many of these people to be deported to Nova Scotia.

question.leadin: Answer the following related to the renormalization of US-Cuba relations.
question.text: This American, who had been imprisoned by the Cuban government since 2009 after bringing communications equipment to Cuban Jews, was freed in 2014.

swap.leadin: Two professors at Harvard Law School rescheduled this activist's last exams to prevent the 1921 class from having a mixed-race, Puerto Rican valedictorian.
swap.text: Name this early 20th-century leader in the Puerto Rican Independence Movement who exposed the racist letters of Dr. Cornelius Rhoads. With colleagues like Blanca Canales, he coordinated the 1950 nationalist revolts.

question.leadin: Alleging fraud after his loss in the 1970 general election, this dictator's supporters mobilized an armed wing of his National Popular Alliance, or ANAPO.
question.text: Name this military dictator of Colombia who was backed by the M-19 movement. This man's 1957 removal by the bipartisan National Front is said to have marked the end of La Violencia.

swap.leadin: After ditching US military school, this man proceeded to buy so many luxury cars for Hollywood actresses that women in Los Angeles began applying bumper stickers reading "THIS CAR WAS NOT A GIFT FROM [him]."
swap.text: Name this infamous playboy and short serving Generalissimo, who ultimately killed both himself and the Duchess of Albuquerque in a car crash while exiled in Madrid. He went by the name of an operatic priest to differentiate him from his father.
swap.answerHtml: Ramfis Trujillo [or Rafael Leónidas Trujillo Martínez; prompt on partial answers; reject “Rafael Trujillo” or “Rafael Leónidas Trujillo Molina”]
